sites.rationale: PIGR has exactly one extracellular terminus: the mature N-terminus (residue 19, K) exposed after cleavage of the 18-residue signal peptide. The 'FLAG-tagged xlPIGR' naming convention (tag-protein) parallels the 'Myc-tagged hA1R' example in the instructions and implies N-terminal placement; because the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus, the topology-derived rule places the junction at residue 18/19. Python confirmed residue 18 = T and residue 19 = K, and the tag site is 621 residues from the TM boundary (640), well clear of any TM constraint. Confidence is low because the ortholog is Xenopus laevis (indirect), no terminus is stated explicitly, and no surface expression or functional assay is reported in the clip. FLAG-tagged full-length xlPIGR (Xenopus laevis PIGR ortholog) transfected into HEK-293 cells (PMC8563443). No residue is named in the clip. The naming convention 'FLAG-tagged xlPIGR' (tag-protein format) implies N-terminal placement. PIGR is a Type I single-pass transmembrane protein with exactly one extracellular terminus: the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 19, after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 18. The tag therefore maps to insert_after_residue=18 by topology. Evidence is indirect (Xenopus ortholog).
